Commentary.Commentary: That concludes a fine competition between bat and ball that was reminiscent of the pre-T20 era. South Africa have dominated their guests so far but Australia have one last chance to avoid a whitewash. The two sides will meet for the final ODI of the 5-match series in Cape Town. Do join at 1700 IST on the 12th of October as we cover all the action then. Until then, cheers and take care!

Kyle Abbott, Man of the Match says that it was a great thing to get an opportunity and come back as hard as that. (On his bowling) He says that it was quite nervy to bowl after a long time but was happy as it paid off for the team.  (On all crucial wickets) He states that it is important to get wickets with the new ball and to get those big players out is a big thing. (On the conditions) He adds that it was a bit different and was a real challenge to bowl here.

Victorious South African skipper, Faf du Plessis says that he found it amazing to go up 4-0 in the series. Adds that they placed Australia under pressure and hammered down on them. Is proud the young players stepped up to perform and the execution of their plan was amazing. Elaborates that Kyle Abbott at the front set the tone and Tabraiz Shamsi spun his web of spin and the bowlers were always on the attack and taking wickets. (On Aaron Phangiso) Du Plessis says he bowled really well too, stayed in good areas and came back well after going for a few runs early on. Says that it is good to have three spinners to play with in different conditions. Admits the wicket was a tough one but really good in a different way as batsmen had to work really hard for runs. Informs that they wanted to be positive but it was really hard with the variable bounce. Is very happy with 4-0 against a fantastic side like Australia and credits his team for playing well. Ends by saying that it is back to practise for his side and 5-0 is something great that he looks forward to.

Steven Smith, Australia captain says that they wanted to have a complete performance with bat and ball but couldn't do it. (On their target) He says that the wicket was not that great and 250 could have been a good target. (On their bowling) He opines that they started well but couldn't hold on till the end as the score was too little to defend. Ends by saying that they will play hard to avoid a whitewash.

Earlier in the day, Australia were beset by the pace and spin duo of Kyle Abbott and Tabraiz Shamsi. Abbott picked up four wickets, two of which came early on and immediately put Australia on the back foot. Shamsi looked very comfortable on the slower pitch, with three dismissals to his name. Mitchell Marsh and Matthew Wade put up fifties each but it was not enough as they couldn't find support from the other batsmen. The tourists ended on a paltry total as they could not stem the loss of wickets.

The Aussie bowlers knew they were in for a hard task as they had a rather low total to defend but they impressed with their bowling discipline. Their lines and lengths were tight and they hemmed the batsmen all the way. The pressure got to the fielding side on a few occasions though, and they left chances that could have been converted into valuable wickets. They got off to a great start thanks to Chris Tremain's early double wicket haul but South Africa buckled down and didn't allow many more wickets to fall. Scott Boland bowled very well too, but didn't have any scalps to show for it.

This is a joyous moment for South Africa, whose win takes the scoreline to 4-0 in the ODI series. This time around, it was a low-scoring affair but both sides put in intense effort. South Africa didn't appear to be in trouble for the most part but the credit for that goes to the stand-in skipper, Faf du Plessis. He anchored the majority of the innings, scoring 69 and batting through two fifty-plus run partnerships, the first with JP Duminy and the other with Rilee Rossouw. The Proteas were frustrated by the bowlers but kept on adding runs to the scoreboard while taking care to marshal their wickets.

Tad short outside off, Behardien gets back and punches iT to mid on for a single.

Full ball outside off, Rossouw punches it through covers for a single. 150 up for the Proteas.

The ball gets the connection but is straight to the man in deep mid-wicket. Travis Head who is nicely set at the ropes takes an easy catch. With that the skipper has to go back to the pavilion. The umpire checks if the fielder was inside the rope. Also they check the no ball. All looks okay. Australia have taken an important wicket but maybe it is too late.
FOUR! In the gap! Full ball outside off, Faf drives it superbly through the covers and the ball races across the ropes.
Shortish outside off, cut to point.
FOUR! 50-RUN STAND BETWEEN DU PLESSIS AND ROSSOUW! Short ball on off, du Plessis attacks that, pulling it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Marsh back on.
Flatter delivery on the stumps, flicked through the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Served outside off, du Plessis rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball through the off side for a single.

NOT OUT! Loopy ball outside off,  du Plessis looks to play it but misses and Warner at slip catches it. Warner appeals and there is some doubt from the Australian side but they decide to review it anyway. The replays show that there was a big gap between bat and ball and the batsman is safe. The sound heard can easily be attributed to the bat hitting the pad.
Australia have reviewed a catching appeal against du Plessis.
Flighted on off, played to the covers for a single.
Zampa to roll his arm.
Length ball outside off, defended with soft hands to point. Just 38 needed now.
Fullish ball outside off, helped to backward point for a single.
Fullish ball on middle, flicked off the pads for a single.
FOUR! DRILLED! Faf does it again! Full outside off, driven through point. The fielder chases after it but there is no real threat as it crosses the boundary. Wonderful stroke play from the skipper.

Length ball on the stumps, punched off the back foot.
Full ball outside off, driven through the covers. One run from the over.
Short ball outside off, Rossouw looks to pull it but the ball goes over to the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Length ball outside off, cut to the off side.
Length ball outside off, guided to third man for a single.

NOT OUT! DECISION OVERTURNED! Short ball on the stumps, du Plessis looks to pull it but the ball passes above the bat and is caught by the keeper.  The fielding side makes a half-hearted appeal and the umpire is quick to raise his finger. Du Plessis doesn't miss a heartbeat and reviews it confidently. The replays show his confidence is well placed as there was no edge at all. There was a sound though so that could lead to confusion on the umpire's part.
The umpire has given Faf du Plessis caught out but the batsman has reviewed the decision.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Fuller ball outside off, tighter length to not give Rilee space, pushed to the covers.

FOUR! SQUIRTED! Fullish ball slightly outside off, Rilee frees his arms and puts it away through backward point. That was hit hard and Rilee shakes his arm to get rid of the shock waves that seem to have jarred his injured little finger.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.
Fuller ball outside off, RR looks to drive and gets a bottom edge that goes to the keeper.
Length ball outside off, defended to the off side. The batsmen run a quick single and just about get away with it.
Boland back on.
Another short delivery outside off, Rossouw lets it through.
Fuller ball outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Bouncer! Faf does well to leave that bouncer.
23rd ODI fifty for Faf du Plessis.
50 for Faf du Plessis! Full on middle, flicked smartly through mid-wicket the batsmen push for a brace and get it. Quality innings from the skipper so far.
Length ball outside off, defended to point.
Back of a length ball outside off, punched off the back foot to the fielder at extra cover.
Yorker on off, Rilee digs it out to mid on. Change-up from Tremain to end the over.
Full outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full delivery on off, driven through mid off.
Short ball on the stumps, pulled away through the leg side for a single.
Length ball outside off, du Plessis guides it with soft hands to backward point for a single.
Shortish ball around off, du Plessis pulls it to the leg side. Good stop by Marsh at short mid-wicket saves the runs.
Full around off, driven to the man at the covers.
Good length ball outside off, du Plessis helps it to third man for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Length ball angled in, du Plessis looks to play it but is hit low on the pads. The ball goes past the keeper to fine leg and the batsmen run a couple. The Umpire signals leg byes.
FOUR! Placement is key! Fuller length ball angled a bit into the skipper, Faf drives it through mid off. That was a brilliantly placed shot, not hit that hard, and makes it across the ropes.
Back of a length ball outside off, played off the back foot to the covers.
Mitchell Marsh will bowl next.
The ball has been square driven by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Fullish ball on middle and off, RR looks to play it off the front foot. The ball nips back in and takes an inside edge to the leg side for a single.
Full on middle and off, driven back to the bowler.
Length ball outside off, du Plessis opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man for a single.

FOUR! SUBLIME! 100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA! Full outside off, Faf leans forward and drives it through wide covers for a boundary. His timing was perfect and so was his placement. That was a beautiful shot to behold!
Fullish ball a tad outside off, defended to point.

Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Yorker on middle, RR does well to dig it out.
Tremain back on.
Outside off, du Plessis has played it to the point region.
Rossouw gets off the mark straight away, driving that full delivery to mid on for a single.

The ball goes to Mitchell Marsh who is waiting at mid off. He reacts fast and takes a crisp two-handed cup catch. This is a big break for Australia.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Tossed up around off, du Plessis gets down on knee and clobbers it hard to mid-wicket. Bailey gets a hand up in time to slow that ball enough and the batsmen get a brace out of it.
Fuller ball outside off, pushed to the covers for a single.
Full on the stumps, driven with soft hands to mid on. The batsmen take a quick single. That looks like a real run out chance but the pressure gets to Smith, who fails to pick it up.
Full on middle and off, driven to mid on.

Fuller ball on middle and leg, defended off the front foot.

Flighted ball outside off, du Plessis punches it through covers for a single.

Tossed up ball outside off, du Plessis slams that to short cover.
Adam Zampa to roll his arm.
Length ball on middle and off, Faf plays it to point for a single.

Length ball outside off, Duminy steers it fine to third man for a single.

Leg bye! Hurls in a length ball on middle and off, Faf moves across to flick that but gets off a thigh pad to fine leg. Leg bye signalled..
Length ball outside off, played to point.

Length ball on off, Faf punches it through the off side for a single.
Tad short outside off, Faf cuts it to point.
Similar ball and Faf plays it to square leg for another brace.
Fuller ball on the pads, Faf Flicks it to square leg for a brace.
FOUR! EDGED! Length ball outside off, Duminy looks to cut it but the ball takes a bottom edge and goes just beyond the keeper and across the third man boundary.

Length delivery, defended from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, pushed to the covers.

DROPPED! Zampa drops a sitter! Shortish ball on middle and off, du Plessis charges down the track and lofts it. The ball goes high over the covers off the top edge. There is a shout for "catch it!" and Adam Zampa is well positioned to do so. He cups his hands but the ball slips through. Single taken. The pressure got to Zampa and that was a massive opportunity lost.
Fullish ball on middle and off, pushed to the covers.
Hastings back on.
Full outside off, driven to the covers. The batsmen must be feeling frustrated now with the lack of runs on offer.
Length ball on off, defended to mid off.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, pushed to the covers for a single.
Length ball outside off, played to point.
Fullish ball on the stumps, worked to mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball outside off and du Plessis half-pulls it to the leg side for a single.
Shortish ball around off, awkwardly pulled by JP to mid-wicket for a single.
Another fuller in length ball, slower one, driven to mid off.

Fullish ball on middle and leg, Duminy looks to drive it but the ball goes off the inside edge and rides up his pads to go to the off side. There was an LBW appeal from the fielding side which was instantly turned down by the umpire.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.

Fullish ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot.
The stadium is resounding with the sounds of the crowds singing the songs played by the band.

Full ball outside off, played to mid off.

Full ball on off, driven through the covers.
Duminy picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Australia are bowling really tight lines and lengths. The South African team has been on the back foot as last 12 balls bowled are dots. Good pressure bowling from the visiting side.
Length ball on off, Duminy looks to block it but is hit high on the thigh pad.
Short ball outside off, du Plessis cuts it a bit late and the ball takes a bottom edge to the off side.
Shortish ball outside off, punched off the back foot to cover.
Full on middle and leg, worked through to short fine leg.
Back of a length ball around off, du Plessis moves back, makes room and punches the ball to the covers.
Length ball outside off, punched to Marsh at extra cover who does well to stop it.
Fullish ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot back to the bowler.

Fuller ball on middle and off, defended to point.
Fuller ball on the pads, flicked to Bailey at mid-wicket who stops it on one bounce.

Full on the stumps, blocked with the full face of the bat from inside the crease.

The players and umpires are back out in the middle. Faf du Plessis and JP Duminy will continue the run chase while Scott Boland will resume the bowling attack.

It's time for lunch at Port Elizabeth. Australia are trying hard to hold the hosts back and it is already paying dividends. Tremain is on a roll, having picked up the wickets of both openers but the bowlers will be feeling the pressure of the scoreboard. South Africa are off to a good start but will have to keep a hold on their wickets, especially on a pitch such as this. Do join us in a short while for the remaining of chase.
Wide outside off, Duminy gets a bottom edge and the ball goes to third man for a single.
Length ball outside off, played with an angled bat to third man for a single.
Full outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Shortish ball outside off, punched to point. Warner is like a gun in the position, as the commentator says, and stops it.
Duminy has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
JP Duminy is the next man in.

It looks like it will go all the way, he has hit it with the wind too but that ball goes straight into the hands of Adam Zampa in the deep who pouches it. South Africa have lost both openers.

Du Plessis survives! Fuller ball outside off, Faf slashes his bat at it and gets a top edge. The ball goes skyward to third man and the ball falls just short of Hastings at third man. Lucky break for Faf! Both the batsmen were ball watching and didn't take any run.

Full ball on off, du Plessis launches into a textbook drive to the man at mid off.

The players are back on  the field. Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock to open. Chris Tremain to bowl.
